_README: canonical_spec_language.json -- the frozen definition of 'canonical' for the
LANGUAGE task. Read by more/run_context.py:assert_not_silent_proxy() when
resolve_task(resolved) == 'language'. The arithmetic task keeps reading
canonical_spec.json, byte-unchanged.
WHY A SECOND FILE RATHER THAN A `task` BLOCK INSIDE canonical_spec.json.
canonical_spec.json is the definition the published arithmetic study is quoted
against, and the guard is not its only reader: export_results.py reads
enforced_fields.dataset_version and .train_split_version, and the
test_phase6_provenance.py / test_phase6_seeding.py gates parse the file
directly and assert on its shape (run_name_template, seed_set). Restructuring
it to hold two tasks would put all of those on the same commit as a language
change, for no scientific gain. T-L1.3 therefore adds a file and touches
nothing.
SAME CONTRACT as canonical_spec.json. A run may declare
logging.experiment_group == 'canonical_lang_b' only if:
(a) every non-null field in enforced_fields matches its resolved config,
(b) every non-null field in architecture_variants[<its architecture>]
matches -- only ITS OWN block is consulted,
(c) resolve_variant() returns `canonical_variant` below (no ablation active),
(d) it uses the full dataset and names a seed from seed_set.
A null means NOT YET FROZEN and refuses any canonical claim that depends on
it. A null in enforced_fields blocks all three arms; a null in one
architecture_variants block blocks only that architecture.
WHY canonical_variant IS 'language' AND NOT 'canonical'. config.py:
resolve_variant returns the task name for a deviation-free language run, so
`variant` can never read 'canonical' for a run that is not the arithmetic
study -- the fifteen published phaseB_* runs own that word (T-L1.1). The check
is exactly as strong: a language run with any deviation resolves to
'language+<tag>', which is not equal to 'language' and is refused.
WHY THE GROUP NAME DIFFERS FROM THE ARITHMETIC ONE. A language run declaring
'canonical_phase_b' is REFUSED outright rather than quietly stamped
exploratory (run_context.py, cross-task group check). 'canonical_phase_b' is
the group export_results.py admits into the headline arithmetic table; a
language run in it would be a row comparing a per-token cross-entropy against
an arithmetic MSE.
WHY SO MANY NULLS. Nothing about the language arm has been measured yet: the
corpus is not built (Phase L-2), the model does not exist (Phase L-4), and no
run has been executed. Every non-null value below is DEFINITIONAL -- a
consequence of the architecture or of plan_language.md's frozen protocol --
rather than selected. See frozen_by, which says which of the two each one is.
_NULLS_NOTE: TASKS_LANGUAGE.md T-L1.3 named eight fields to leave null: epochs,
batch_size, lr, weight_decay, seq_len, max_depth, primary_metric_floor and
ffn_mult.mor. This file leaves MORE than eight null, and the additions are
deliberate, so they are named here rather than discovered later:
routing_balance_weight (moe, more) and halting_weight (mor, more) were
selected at T4.2 against ARITHMETIC magnitudes: 0.001 was chosen because it
put the weighted balance term at 0.017x the task loss after warmup. The
language task loss is a per-token cross-entropy near ln(8192) = 9.0 nats at
initialisation, against arithmetic's ~0.06 MSE -- more than two orders of
magnitude larger. The same 0.001 would put the balance term at ~1e-4 x the
task loss, i.e. effectively OFF, in the arm whose central failure mode is
router collapse; and the ponder cost would be equally invisible against a
loss that large, which would silently turn adaptive depth into always-max
depth. Carrying those numbers over would not be reuse -- it would be an
untested assumption wearing a frozen number's authority. They stay null
until a language T4.2 measures them the same way.
dropout, for the opposite reason: 0.1 was INHERITED on arithmetic (70k
records, a regime where it was never load-bearing). WikiText-103 is ~103 M
training tokens against a ~3.2 M-parameter model, so the language arm is
underfitting by construction and 0.1 is a guess in the wrong direction. Not
frozen until measured.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT from enforced_fields, compared with
canonical_spec.json: max_steps and step_feat_dim. Those are arithmetic dataset
properties (7 step-tokens x 12 features). The shared config defaults still
fill them into a resolved language config -- see the OWED TO L-4 note in
config.py:_apply_language_block -- but enforcing them here would freeze an
arithmetic dataset shape into the definition of a language run.
HOW TO FREEZE A FIELD: replace the null with the measured value AND add its
one-line justification to frozen_by in the same edit, naming the task or gate
that produced it. A frozen number with no frozen_by entry is indistinguishable
from an inherited guess, which is the failure this file exists to prevent.
_T_L7_1_FREEZE_NOTE: T-L7.1 CLOSED EVERY REMAINING NULL IN ONE EDIT. Read this before changing any
number below: the fields are not independent, and the reason each one is what it
is lives in frozen_by / architecture_variants_frozen_by, one entry per field.
THE HEADLINE RESULT OF THE CALIBRATION IS A REJECTION, NOT A TRANSFER. The
_NULLS_NOTE above predicted that the arithmetic 0.001 loss weights would be
'effectively OFF' against a ~5-nat cross-entropy and that the fix was to re-scale
them to the same 0.017x-of-task-loss RATIO T4.2 used. That prediction was
MEASURED AND IS FALSE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The ratio-matched values (0.21
balance, 0.107 halting) are worse than 0.001 on val/task_loss AND on routing AMI,
and at halting 0.107 average depth collapses to 1.49 of a 7 budget while AMI falls
0.2907 -> 0.0025 -- i.e. the ratio rule switches OFF both behaviours this study
exists to measure. The invariant carried from arithmetic is ABSOLUTE GRADIENT
MAGNITUDE, not the ratio to task loss: 0.017x of a 0.06 MSE is a nudge, 0.017x of
a 5-nat cross-entropy is ~100x that in absolute terms, against a task loss that
cannot be driven to zero. Full grids in code/lang_calibration_weights.json and
code/lang_calibration_reg.json.
EVERY CALIBRATION NUMBER WAS MEASURED ON wikitext-2, THE DEV CORPUS, AND MAY
NEVER BE QUOTED AS A RESULT. wikitext-2 shares its validation split byte-for-byte
with wikitext-103 (T-L2.0), so a dev-corpus val loss is not a held-out number for
the canonical corpus. It is legitimate for SELECTING a hyperparameter and illegitimate
for reporting one. The floor those runs are read against is the dev corpus's own
3 epochs, seq_len 256, batch 64, seed 44, one axis at a time. batch 64 was the
calibration batch and 48 is the frozen one: the selection is a comparison BETWEEN
grid points at a fixed batch, so it does not transfer a batch-dependent optimum,
and the two throughput regimes are 6 GB-specific (T-L7.0) rather than a property
of the weights.

frozen_by.epochs: FROZEN AT 3 BY T-L7.1, AND THIS IS A BUDGET DECISION STATED AS ONE RATHER THAN A CONVERGENCE CLAIM. The arithmetic 50 does not transfer: one epoch here is 526,320 blocks x 256 = 134,737,920 tokens, against 70 k records. From the T-L7.0 per-arm timings at batch 48 (MoE 0.41, MoR 1.03, MoRE 1.16 h/epoch on the 3050), the full 3 x 5 matrix costs 39.0 h at 3 epochs and 26.0 h at 2. 3 was chosen over 2 for a measurable reason, not for headroom: the halting axis needs more than two epochs to separate the arms at all -- in the calibration grid average depth was still moving between epochs 2 and 3 on every point, so a 2-epoch matrix would report a depth allocation that had not finished forming and would understate MoRE's adaptive behaviour in the one place the paper's claim lives. Going to 8 epochs (~104 h) was rejected on cost, not on evidence, and the honest phrasing for the paper is that these are FIXED-BUDGET runs at 3 epochs over ~135 M tokens, not runs trained to convergence. Every arm gets the identical budget, so the comparison is valid even though no arm is converged.
frozen_by.batch_size: FROZEN AT 48 BY T-L7.0/T-L7.1, MEASURED PER ARM, AND TUNED FOR THE 8 GB CARD THAT RUNS THE MATRIX. Not the largest batch that fits: MoR is the memory-heavy arm (ffn_mult 24) and it sets the ceiling, peaking at 5,342 MiB at batch 48 against MoE's 1,914 and MoRE's 3,098. That is 87% of the 3050's 6 GB and 65% of the 4060's 8 GB, so one number serves both machines and the gate machine can reproduce a matrix run. Batch 64 was measured and REJECTED even though it is faster for MoE and MoRE: MoR's peak goes to 7,338 MiB, crosses the 6 GB line into the T-L7.0 soft-cliff regime, and its epoch time goes UP from 1.03 h to 2.31 h -- so batch 64 costs 57.0 h of matrix wall-clock against batch 48's 39.0 h. Batch 32 fits everywhere (3,225 MiB) but is slower on every arm (46.3 h). 48 is the measured optimum, and the choice is recorded here rather than in a changelog because a later agent raising it to 64 'because 8 GB has room' would silently re-enter the cliff. NOT MEASURED: whether the 4060 holds MoR at batch 64 at 89.6% of 8 GB -- see HANDOFF.md, which probes that card before the matrix starts. The frozen value does not depend on the answer.
frozen_by.subset_fraction: DEFINITIONAL. CLAUDE.md 5 / plan.md Gate 0: a canonical run is never a subset run. Identical to the arithmetic spec.
frozen_by.num_blocks: DEFINITIONAL. plan_language.md 6.5: ONE shared block reused across recursion steps. More than one block is a stack, which is the thing MoR is defined against.
frozen_by.dataset_version: FROZEN BY T-L7.1 AT lang-wikitext-103-bpe8192-len256-800d6154, now that seq_len is frozen at 256 -- the string encodes seq_len (-len256-), which is why it waited. MEASURED, not declared: derived in build_language_dataset.py from the per-split content hashes (T-L2.7c) over 134,737,951 train tokens / 526,320 blocks at V=8192, HF revision b08601e04326, tokenizer sha256 6a1f1477f4d9. RELATED DEFECT, fixed in T-L7.1a and worth knowing before trusting any pre-T-L7.1a language run: the resolved config used to carry the ARITHMETIC string more6-v1-seed42-n70000-3c1087b6aad9 in this field while reading WikiText, because both version strings came from config.json's shared data block and MoRELanguageDataset -- which knows the right answer -- is constructed inside engine.train(), after RunContext.create has already hashed the config and stamped provenance. config.py:stamp_language_dataset_versions now writes the corpus's own strings before the guard runs. Consequence: every language run in runs/ created before that fix reports the wrong dataset id in provenance and cannot be admitted by export_results.py, which filters on this field; their measured numbers are not wrong, their label is. SUPERSEDED TEXT, kept because it records why the field waited: 'STILL NULL, and after T-L2.7 that is a decision rather than an omission. The corpus IS built and Gate L2 passes on it: data/lang/wikitext-103/ carries V=8192, 134,737,951 train tokens, 526,320 blocks, dataset_version lang-wikitext-103-bpe8192-len256-800d6154. It is not frozen here because the version string encodes seq_len (-len256-), and seq_len is Gate L5's to decide from measured throughput and VRAM headroom -- see this field's neighbour below. Freezing the version now would either pre-empt that measurement or guarantee a re-freeze after it. The fetch and tokenizer stages ARE settled (HF revision b08601e04326, tokenizer sha256 6a1f1477f4d9), so only the packing is open. The guard still refuses every canonical claim while this is null, which is correct: no language run may enter a table before Gate L5.'
frozen_by.train_split_version: FROZEN BY T-L7.1 AT wikitext-author-splits-v1, the constant MoRELanguageDataset already exposed. It records that the run used WikiText's AUTHOR-PROVIDED, document-disjoint splits rather than a re-split of the corpus -- T-L2.7 verified the consequence directly: zero exact-content overlap between train and val/test across all 526,320 canonical train blocks. The reason this was null until now was plumbing, not measurement, and the plumbing is the T-L7.1a fix described under dataset_version: the string is stamped into cfg[data] by config.py:stamp_language_dataset_versions BEFORE RunContext.create hashes the config, because the dataset object that knows it is not constructed until engine.train(). Unlike dataset_version it does not encode seq_len, so a repack would not move it.
frozen_by.seq_len: FROZEN BY T-L7.1 AT 256, and the number equals config.py's provisional LANGUAGE_SEQ_LEN_DEFAULT by measurement rather than by copying -- which is the distinction this entry previously insisted on. T-L7.0 swept 128/256/512 per arm on the actual GPU. 256 is where all three arms fit a common batch with headroom on the 6 GB card (worst-arm peak 5,342 MiB at batch 48) while giving each token 255 tokens of causal context; 512 roughly doubles the activation footprint and forces MoR's batch down far enough that the matrix gets slower, and 128 halves the context a language model has to work with for a throughput gain that does not change the verdict. Coupled to dataset_version, which encodes it: changing seq_len requires a repack and a new dataset id, so this is the field a later agent is most likely to move by accident. It is INDEPENDENT of mor.ffn_mult -- 128/256/512/1024 all derive 24 (T-L6.3).
frozen_by.lr: FROZEN BY T-L7.1 AT 0.001, MEASURED on language rather than inherited, which the previous NULL text correctly insisted on: an MSE regression head and a per-token softmax over 8192 classes are different optimisation problems, so the arithmetic 0.001 being the same number is a coincidence that had to be earned. The 3 x 2 (lr, dropout) grid at 3 epochs on the dev corpus gives val/task_loss 5.2406 at 1e-3, 5.5774 at 5e-4 and 5.3248 at 2e-3 (dropout 0.0; the dev bigram floor is 5.3983). So 5e-4 does not reach the floor in the budget at all, and 2e-3 is unstable rather than merely worse: at 2e-3 with dropout 0.1 the run diverged to 7.1957 -- above the UNIGRAM ce and with average depth pinned at the 7.0 ceiling, the signature of a model that has stopped learning and is pondering everything. 1e-3 is the only value that is both best and stable across both dropout settings. Grid in code/lang_calibration_reg.json.
frozen_by.weight_decay: FROZEN BY T-L7.1 AT 0.0001, and this one is CARRIED, NOT MEASURED -- stated plainly because the field sits next to two that were measured and would otherwise borrow their authority. The (lr, dropout) grid held weight_decay fixed at 1e-4, so there is no language evidence distinguishing it from 0 or from 1e-3. It is frozen only so the matrix has one definition and every arm shares it. The caveat the NULL text raised is still live and still unmeasured: with tie_lm_head true, weight decay now acts on the output projection as well as the embedding, which it did not on arithmetic. If a reviewer asks whether the language result is sensitive to it, the honest answer is that it was not swept, and the experiment is a labelled one-axis ablation at fixed lr 1e-3, not a re-freeze.
frozen_by.dropout: FROZEN AT 0.1 BY THE USER'S EXPLICIT PROTOCOL DECISION (2026-09-06), AGAINST A MEASUREMENT THAT MARGINALLY FAVOURS 0.0 -- recorded this way round on purpose, because a frozen number whose provenance is a choice must not read as a measurement. The grid: at lr 1e-3, dropout 0.0 gives val/task_loss 5.2406 and dropout 0.1 gives 5.2543, a gap of 0.0137 nats at ONE seed on the dev corpus, which is inside plausible seed noise and is not a result. At lr 5e-4 the gap is 0.0014 nats, i.e. nothing. The one place dropout is not neutral is stability: the only diverged point in the whole grid is lr 2e-3 with dropout 0.1 (7.1957, depth pinned at 7.0), and that is an argument about lr 2e-3, which is not frozen. The theoretical argument still points at 0.0 and is unchanged from _NULLS_NOTE -- 526,320 blocks x 256 tokens x 3 epochs against ~3.4 M non-embedding parameters is an underfitting regime where regularisation has no job -- so the measured and theoretical preference agree with each other and disagree with the frozen value by ~0.01 nats. Frozen at 0.1 anyway because the choice is the user's to make, it costs less than the seed-to-seed spread this study will report, and matching the arithmetic study's dropout removes one axis of difference between the two tasks. TO REVISIT IT: it is a one-line labelled ablation at 0.0, not a re-freeze, and the matrix must not be re-run for it.
frozen_by.vocab_size: DEFINITIONAL-BY-PROTOCOL. 8192, byte-level BPE fitted on the TRAINING SPLIT ONLY (T-L2.1). Chosen for a stated reason rather than tuned: GPT-2's 50257 would put a 12.9 M-parameter embedding table in front of a ~3.2 M-parameter expert stack, so the study would be measuring the embedding, not the architecture. Tied to dataset_version -- changing it invalidates the tokenized corpus, and Gate L2 checks the two agree.
frozen_by.d_model: DEFINITIONAL-BY-PROTOCOL. 256, identical to the arithmetic study and identical across all three language arms, so MoE/MoR/MoRE differ only in the axes CLAUDE.md 1 defines. Not re-tuned for language; a width sweep would be a separate labelled experiment.
frozen_by.n_heads: DEFINITIONAL-BY-PROTOCOL. 4 at d_model 256 (plan_language.md 6.6), frozen identically across the three arms. Attention hyperparameters are protocol, not per-architecture tuning, because MoR keeping attention is the whole point: one expert is not the same as no context.
frozen_by.attention: DEFINITIONAL. plan_language.md 6.5. attention=False constructs no attention module at all, i.e. a model in which no token can see any other token -- not a weaker language model but a different object. There is no legitimate language run with it off, in any arm, including MoR.
frozen_by.tie_lm_head: DEFINITIONAL-BY-PROTOCOL. plan_language.md 5: the output projection is the token embedding transposed. Untying would add 2 x V x d_model parameters that differ across arms only through the shared trunk, diluting the parameter-budget match the comparison depends on. Untied is available as a labelled ablation.
frozen_by.grad_clip: INHERITED-STABILITY, frozen at 1.0. Not a tuned quantity and not a scientific claim -- a global-norm ceiling that prevented no observed blowup on arithmetic and is kept so a language divergence is a real divergence rather than an unclipped step. Stated as inherited, never as selected.
frozen_by.routing_mode: DEFINITIONAL. updated_rules.md 1.1 / plan.md 4.1. Top-1 sparse dispatch; dense evaluate-all-and-blend is the labelled ablation and may never be canonical, on either task.
frozen_by.router_noise: DEFINITIONAL. updated_rules.md 2.5. Canonical default is none on both tasks; exploration noise is a labelled ablation.
frozen_by.halting_mode: CARRIED, and this one is a genuine inheritance from a measurement on the OTHER task: T8.0a's controlled arithmetic experiment selected pure_act over supervised_curriculum under a pre-registered tie rule. On language the choice is additionally FORCED -- a supervised curriculum needs a per-item oracle depth, and a packed LM sequence has no per-token complexity label to build one from (plan_language.md 7.3). So pure_act here is not a transferred hyperparameter, it is the only defined option; supervised_curriculum is not available on language at all.
frozen_by.task_weight: DEFINITIONAL. loss_weights.task = 1.0 is the reference scale the other weights are expressed against, on both tasks. Not tuned.
frozen_by.family_cls_weight: DEFINITIONAL AND REQUIRED 0.0, and it is the most load-bearing entry here. plan_language.md 7.3: on language the family head reads h.detach(), so its gradient reaches only its own Linear and its weight cannot change what the trunk learns. A non-zero value would record a supervision term that does not exist. The scientific consequence is a STRENGTHENING over the arithmetic study, where a 6-way family cross-entropy was the second-largest term in the objective and every specialization claim has to be caveated for it: here no family signal enters the trunk at any weight, so routing accuracy, AMI and purity measure EMERGENT structure. cli.py refuses --family_cls with any non-zero value on language rather than ignoring it.

_note: Only the block whose name equals the run's `architecture` is consulted, so a
null in mor.ffn_mult blocks canonical MoR without blocking MoE or MoRE.
`top1_routing` is descriptive only (run_context.py:
_ARCH_VARIANT_DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY): the enforceable facts behind it are
routing_mode, shared above, and num_experts, enforced here.
`attention` is NOT here even though a reader might expect it per-arm -- it
is in enforced_fields, shared by all three. That placement is the claim:
MoR keeps causal self-attention. One expert is a statement about WHICH
computation, not about whether a token may see its context, and a MoR arm
without attention would make every MoR-vs-MoRE number a comparison of
context access instead of a comparison of routing.
mor.ffn_mult IS NULL, unlike the arithmetic spec's 24. The policy carries
over -- equalise total FFN hidden width, not the per-FFN multiplier -- but
the arithmetic value cannot: 24 = 4 x 6 made MoR's single FFN match the six
experts' combined width and landed within 0.12% of MoRE's TOTAL parameter
count, and that residual was computed for a model with no attention
sublayer and no 8192 x 256 tied embedding. Both of those are now shared,
identical additions to all three arms, so they move the total each arm is
matched on and therefore move which integer multiplier minimises the gap.
It must be re-measured against T9.2's 5% bound before any language run
claims canonical status; 24 is the starting hypothesis, not the answer.
max_depth IS NULL for mor and more. On arithmetic it was 7 because that
matched max_steps -- a DATASET property (programs are packed with 7
step-tokens). Language has no per-item step count, so the recursion budget
has no dataset to inherit from and is a real choice with a real cost: it
multiplies compute per token. moe.max_depth stays 1 because MoE is defined
by having no recursion at all.

architecture_variants_frozen_by.num_experts: DEFINITIONAL. Six families is the arithmetic manifest's number and is CARRIED, not derived: language has no operation families, so six is a capacity choice, and the honest statement is that it is held at six so MoE/MoRE keep the same router width the arithmetic study used. MoR is 1 by definition (no routing decision).
architecture_variants_frozen_by.max_depth: FROZEN BY T-L7.1 AT 7 for mor/more; moe is 1 by definition (MoE has no recursion). CARRIED FROM ARITHMETIC BY BUDGET, NOT BY DERIVATION, and the distinction matters because on arithmetic 7 was a DATASET property (programs are packed with 7 step-tokens) and language has no per-item step count to inherit from. What makes 7 defensible here is that it is a CEILING the model is measured against rather than a target: across the whole calibration grid average depth landed between 1.07 and 2.66 of the 7 available, so the budget is not binding at the frozen loss weights and the halting head is making a real choice instead of saturating. Two failure signatures bracket it -- a depth pinned AT 7.0 is the divergence signature (seen once, at lr 2e-3 with dropout 0.1), and a depth near 1.0 means halting has been over-penalised (seen at halting_weight 0.5, depth 1.07). Cost is the reason not to raise it: max_depth multiplies the recursive FFN compute per token, and it is what makes MoR/MoRE ~2.5x MoE's epoch time (T-L7.0). Keeping the arithmetic value also keeps one fewer axis different between the two tasks, so a MoRE-vs-MoRE cross-task remark is about the data and not about the recursion budget.
architecture_variants_frozen_by.adaptive_halting: DEFINITIONAL. MoR and MoRE have ACT halting, MoE does not. Unchanged from arithmetic.
architecture_variants_frozen_by.ffn_mult: moe/more 4, CARRIED unchanged (hidden width 4 x d_model, the conventional transformer ratio). mor 24, RE-DERIVED for the language shape by code/derive_lang_ffn_mult.py (T-L6.3), not copied: rel(non-embedding) 0.112%, rel(total) 0.069%, and only 23/24/25 satisfy the 5% requirement on both counts. It equals the arithmetic value for a structural reason -- attention and the tied V x d_model embedding are added EQUALLY to every arm and cancel in P_MoR - P_MoRE, leaving the expert-stack condition 6 experts at mult 4 against 1 at mult 24. Insensitive to seq_len (128/256/512/1024 all give 24), so this field and Gate L5's seq_len are independent. Derivation table in code/lang_ffn_mult_derivation.json.
architecture_variants_frozen_by.routing_balance_weight: FROZEN BY T-L7.1 AT 0.001 for moe/more; mor 0.0 is DEFINITIONAL (one expert, nothing to balance). MEASURED ON LANGUAGE, and the measurement REJECTS the re-scaling _NULLS_NOTE predicted would be necessary -- read that note's prediction and then this: it is the same number as arithmetic, arrived at independently, and the near-identity is the finding rather than laziness. One-axis grid at halting 0.001, 3 epochs, dev corpus, val/task_loss then routing AMI: 0.001 -> 5.2406, AMI 0.2907 (its own per-run control floor 0.0621) | 0.05 -> 5.2991, 0.3070 | 0.21 -> 5.3097, 0.2688 | 1.0 -> 5.3458, 0.1807. 0.21 is the value that reproduces T4.2's 0.017x-of-task-loss RATIO, and it is worse than 0.001 on val loss by 0.069 nats AND worse on AMI. So the quantity that transfers across tasks is the ABSOLUTE gradient magnitude of the auxiliary term, not its ratio to a task loss whose scale changed by two orders of magnitude. SECONDARY COHERENCE CHECK, and the reason to trust the low value rather than merely record it: 0.001 sits at normalised load entropy 0.8571, just BELOW the oracle POS partition's own entropy of 0.8884, while every higher weight overshoots to 0.99+ -- i.e. the weight that best matches the balance the data itself has is also the weight that predicts best, and the higher weights are buying uniformity the data does not have. Note the sign of the trade-off for the paper: entropy and AMI move in OPPOSITE directions here, which is exactly why CLAUDE.md 2 forbids tuning toward maximal entropy. Grid in code/lang_calibration_weights.json.
architecture_variants_frozen_by.step_routing_weight: DEFINITIONAL 0.0, and on language it is FORCED rather than chosen. A non-zero value trains the router against an oracle expert index; language has no per-token oracle expert, because there is no operation family to read off a token. The oracle-routing ablation that exists on arithmetic (T10.E) has no language counterpart, so 0.0 is the only defined value in all three blocks.
architecture_variants_frozen_by.halting_weight: FROZEN BY T-L7.1 AT 0.001 for mor/more; moe 0.0 is DEFINITIONAL (at max_depth 1 every token forced-exits at step 1, so a ponder cost would be a constant). MEASURED, and this is the axis where the inherited ratio rule fails hardest -- the entry that used to sit here predicted the arithmetic 0.001 would leave the ponder cost 'invisible against a loss that large' and would 'silently turn adaptive depth into always-max depth'. THE OPPOSITE IS WHAT HAPPENS. One-axis grid at balance 0.001, 3 epochs, dev corpus, val/task_loss | avg depth | AMI: 0.001 -> 5.2406 | 2.63 | 0.2907 (control 0.0621) | 0.03 -> 5.2547 | 2.30 | 0.0050 | 0.107 -> 5.3345 | 1.49 | 0.0025 | 0.5 -> 5.3305 | 1.07 | 0.0205. At 0.001 depth is 2.63 of a 7 budget -- adaptive, not saturated -- and routing structure is 4.7x its own control floor. 0.107 is the ratio-matched value and it is a DOUBLE FAILURE: depth collapses to 1.49, i.e. most tokens exit after one step and MoRE degenerates toward MoE, and AMI falls 0.2907 -> 0.0025, statistically indistinguishable from the shuffled control. The ratio rule does not merely mis-tune this term, it switches off both behaviours the study exists to measure, and it would have produced a clean-looking Outcome C that was an artifact of the loss weight. THE COUPLING IS THE SCIENTIFICALLY INTERESTING PART and belongs in the paper: raising the HALTING weight destroys ROUTING structure, which is not obvious a priori -- with fewer recursion steps the router has fewer opportunities to specialise, so depth and expert differentiation are not independent knobs in MoRE the way they are in MoR and MoE separately. Grid in code/lang_calibration_weights.json.
architecture_variants_frozen_by.halting_supervision_weight: DEFINITIONAL 0.0 everywhere, and FORCED on language for the same reason as step_routing_weight: a supervised halting target needs a per-item oracle depth, and there is no per-token complexity label in a packed LM sequence. The supervised_curriculum ablation does not exist on this task.

_README: The written-down comparison rules for the language matrix. NOT checked by the
Gate 0 guard -- recorded here so there is one source of truth instead of a
convention living in a changelog entry. Where a rule is identical to the
arithmetic one it says so explicitly, because 'the same as arithmetic' is a
claim that has to be true rather than assumed.
protocol.primary_metric_note: Per-token cross-entropy in NATS, mean over the packed validation tokens. Same metric key as arithmetic so the exporter and metric contract need no special case, but a different quantity -- never put the two in one table. Report bits/token (nats / ln 2) and perplexity (exp nats) as derived columns; they are monotone transforms and carry no extra information, so the verdict is always taken on nats. CLAUDE.md 4 still holds: total_loss is never the primary metric.
protocol.primary_metric_floor_note: MEASURED in T-L2.5 on wikitext-103, fitted on train and evaluated on val: uniform_ce = 9.010913 (= ln 8192 exactly, 13.0000 bits), unigram_ce = 7.198213, bigram_ce = 4.984947 nats/token. The floor is the BIGRAM, not the unigram this note originally named: plan_language.md 3 and T-L2.5 require all three and take the LOWEST, because a model that beats only the unigram has not beaten what a two-column count table does. Read val/task_loss against 4.9849 nats (7.1918 bits, perplexity 146.2), never against 0. The ceiling companion is uniform_ce: a run above 9.0109 is broken. Dev-corpus values differ and are not interchangeable -- wikitext-2 gives 5.398 nats because its bigram counts are 50x sparser. Measured at dataset_version lang-wikitext-103-bpe8192-len256-800d6154; a repack at a different seq_len moves these by the dropped-tail fraction only (31 tokens of 134,737,951, ~2e-7 relative), so the number survives a Gate L5 seq_len decision. Not enforced by the Gate 0 guard -- see this block's _README.
protocol.seed_reporting: mean +- std over the full seed_set; verdicts come from the exact two-sided randomization test in code/seed_stats.py, never from a k x std threshold
protocol.seed_reporting_note: IDENTICAL to canonical_spec.json:protocol.seed_reporting, and identical for the same reason -- the correct denominator for a difference of means is the standard error of the difference, and at 5-vs-5 the 252 regroupings let the null distribution be enumerated exactly. Report the resolution floor 1/C(10,5) = 0.0040 alongside every p. Do not re-derive a language-specific rule.
protocol.checkpoint_selection_note: IDENTICAL to the arithmetic rule as amended at T11.0b. The reason transfers unchanged: a minimum over evaluated epochs is an order statistic whose downward bias grows with an arm's per-epoch validation noise, and that noise is not matched across arms, so selecting on it hands the noisiest arm the largest free improvement. best_val_loss stays in metrics.json as a secondary column.
protocol.val_interval_note: FROZEN BY T-L7.1 AT 1 -- validate every epoch, i.e. logging.log_interval = 1. With epochs frozen at 3 there is no other defensible value: at 2 a 3-epoch run gets validation at epochs 2 and 3 only, and checkpoint_selection is final-epoch, so the mid-run curve would be a single point and a divergence in epoch 1 would be invisible until the run was two-thirds spent. Cost is ~1 validation pass per epoch over 5,832 val blocks, negligible against a 1.16 h epoch. CORRECTION OF A FALSE CLAIM THAT USED TO BE IN THIS FIELD, recorded rather than silently deleted: the previous text said 'logging.log_interval enters config_hash: changing it mid-matrix produces two hash groups that may not share a table.' THAT IS WRONG AND WAS VERIFIED WRONG IN T-L7.1. config_hash is SHA-256 over the resolved config with the provenance AND logging blocks REMOVED, so log_interval 2 and log_interval 10 hash identically (both e8a6776b2093f861 on the config tested). The practical consequence is the reverse of what the old note warned about: changing the validation interval mid-matrix does NOT split the hash group, so it will NOT be caught by the exporter's config_hash check and must be caught by reading this field. Set it before the matrix and do not touch it.
protocol.parameter_budget_policy: equalise total FFN hidden width, not per-FFN multiplier
protocol.parameter_budget_note: Policy CARRIED from arithmetic; the multiplier that implements it is NOT (mor.ffn_mult is null). Two shared components now sit in every arm's total and did not exist on arithmetic: the causal self-attention sublayer, shared across recursion depth, and the tied 8192 x 256 token embedding, which is 2.097 M parameters -- comparable to the whole arithmetic model. Because they are IDENTICAL in all three arms they cannot explain any difference between arms, but they do change the denominator of the 5% budget-matching bound, so the bound must be re-checked, not assumed. Report the achieved gap in the results table exactly as the arithmetic study did, including its sign relative to the winning arm.
protocol.attention_is_shared: MoE, MoR and MoRE all use n_heads = 4 causal self-attention at d_model 256, one shared sublayer reused at every recursion step (plan_language.md 6.5-6.6). Recorded in protocol because it is the assumption that makes the three-way comparison mean anything: the arms differ in WHICH expert and HOW MANY steps, never in whether a token can see its context.
